title: Kőnig's theorems and Dilworth's theorem
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Kőnig's edge-colouring theorem: the line graph of a finite bipartite graph G is Δ(G)-colourable, and its chromatic number (the chromatic index of G) equals Δ(G). The proof colours edges one at a time with partial proper edge colourings, recolouring by an a/b Kempe-chain swap whose correctness rests on a parity argument in the bipartite graph; the lower bound comes from the edges at a vertex of maximum degree, which are pairwise adjacent in the line graph. Also formalized: the Kőnig–Egerváry theorem (a finite bipartite graph has a matching and a vertex cover of the same size, via Hall's theorem with deficiency, plus weak duality for all finite graphs), Dilworth's theorem (an antichain A and a partition into |A| chains, by Galvin's induction) and Mirsky's dual theorem (a chain C and a partition into |C| antichains, by the height function).
